questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Tuvalu?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Tuvalu article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Tuvalu?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tuvalu article.

questions.proof: The most important languages spoken in Tuvalu are Tuvaluan and English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was part of Gilbert and Ellice Islands with _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Islands”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tuvalu article.

questions.proof: It was part of Gilbert and Ellice Islands with Kiribati.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The administration of the BWTP ended in _____, and the Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony was established, which existed until October 1975.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Colonial administration” part of the Tuvalu article.

questions.proof: The administration of the BWTP ended in 1916, and the Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony was established, which existed until October 1975.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The United States and Tuvalu signed a treaty of friendship in _____, when the US gave up their claim to Tuvalu for the islands of Funafuti, Nukefetau, Nukulaelae, and Nurakita.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Tuvalu article.

questions.proof: The United States and Tuvalu signed a treaty of friendship in 1979, when the US gave up their claim to Tuvalu for the islands of Funafuti, Nukefetau, Nukulaelae, and Nurakita.
